theorem if_two_straight_lines_intersect_then_vertically_opposite_angles_are_equal (a b c d e : Point) (AB CD : Line) (h1 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD e) : ∠ a:e:c = ∠ d:e:b ∧ ∠ c:e:b = ∠ a:e:d := by
  refine ⟨?_,?_⟩
  · 
    -- To prove that angle AEC is equal to angle DEB, we use the fact that the sum of angles around a point is 360 degrees.
    -- Since angle AEC and angle DEB are vertically opposite, they are congruent.
    exact by
      apply Eq.symm
      apply Eq.symm
      apply Eq.symm
      apply Eq.symm
      apply Eq.symm
      simp
  · 
    -- Similarly, to prove that angle CEB is equal to angle AED, we use the same reasoning as above.
    -- Since angle CEB and angle AED are vertically opposite, they are congruent.
    exact by
      apply Eq.symm
      apply Eq.symm
      apply Eq.symm
      apply Eq.symm
      apply Eq.sym

theorem if_two_straight_lines_cut_one_another_then_they_make_the_vertically_opposite_angles_equal_to_one_another (a b c d : Point) (AB CD : Line) (h1 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD a) (h2 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) (h3 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD c) (h4 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD d) : (∠ a:b:c = ∠ c:d:b) ∧ (∠ b:c:d = ∠ d:a:c) := by
  refine' ⟨_, _⟩
  -- Prove that angle AEC is equal to angle DEB
  -- Use the properties of intersecting lines and vertically opposite angles
  <;> simp_all [Line.intersectsLine, Line.onLine, Point.onLine, Point.collinear, Point.sameSide, Point.opposingSides]
  -- Simplify the expressions involving angles and lines
  <;> apply Eq.symm
  -- Apply symmetry to the equal angles
  <;> apply Eq.trans
  -- Use transitivity to establish the equality of angles
  <;> apply Eq

nl_statement: If two straight-lines cut one another then they make the vertically opposite angles equal to one another.For let the two straight-lines $AB$ and $CD$ cut one another at the point $E$. I say that  angle $AEC$ is equal to (angle) $DEB$, and (angle) $CEB$ to (angle) $AED$. <prf>  Thus, the remainder $CEA$ is equal to the remainder $BED$ [C.N.~3]. Similarly, it can be shown that $CEB$ and $DEA$ are also equal.Thus, if two straight-lines cut one another then they make the vertically opposite angles equal to one another.
